title: Introduction to Derivatives: The Mathematics of Change
subject: math

concepts.name: the_intuition_hook
concepts.instructions: Start by explaining that Calculus is the study of how things change. Use the car speedometer analogy: average speed is easy (distance/time), but the speedometer shows your speed at this exact instant. Use 'show_image' to display a car speedometer. Use 'add_text' to define 'Derivative = Instantaneous Rate of Change' at top-center. Call next_concept().

concepts.name: average_rate_gap
concepts.instructions: Explain that to find a slope, we need two points. This is the Average Rate of Change (slope of a secant line). Use 'show_image' to display a secant line on a curve. Use 'add_text' to show the formula (f(x+h) - f(x)) / h at below-last. Call next_concept().

concepts.name: closing_the_gap
concepts.instructions: Ask what happens if we move the two points closer until they touch. The Secant becomes a Tangent! Use 'show_image' to display a tangent line touching a curve. Use 'add_text' to define the derivative: f'(x) = lim(h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h at below-last. Call next_concept().

concepts.name: spotting_the_pattern
concepts.instructions: Instead of using the limit formula every time, let's find a pattern. Use 'add_text' to show: x^2 -> 2x, x^3 -> 3x^2, x^4 -> 4x^3. Ask the student to guess the rule for x^n. Call next_concept().

concepts.name: power_rule_algorithm
concepts.instructions: Confirm the pattern - this is the Power Rule! Bring the power down and subtract one. Use 'draw_diagram' with type='flowchart' and nodes=['Start: x^n', 'Bring power down', 'Subtract 1 from exponent', 'Result: n*x^(n-1)']. Use 'add_text' to show example: d/dx(x^5) = 5x^4 at below-last. Call next_concept().

concepts.name: linear_behavior
concepts.instructions: Show how this works for straight lines. Use 'show_image' to display a linear function graph. Explain that a line never curves so its slope is constant. Use 'add_text' to show d/dx(2x + 1) = 2 at below-last. The derivative of a linear term is just the coefficient. Call next_concept().

concepts.name: visualizing_slopes
concepts.instructions: The derivative tells us if the function is rising or falling. Use 'show_image' to display a cubic function with peaks and valleys. Point out: when the curve goes up, derivative is positive; when it goes down, derivative is negative. Use 'add_text' to show 'Derivative = 0 at peaks and valleys' at below-last. Call next_concept().

concepts.name: final_cheat_sheet
concepts.instructions: Congratulate the student! Use 'add_text' to summarize the key rules: Power Rule: nx^(n-1), Constant: 0, Linear (cx): c, Sum: f'(x) + g'(x). Emphasize these rules are the foundation of Calculus. Call finish_lesson().
